hypothesis: FP32 normalized composition cells can contain reference-qualified chemistry changes with incompatible GBCT output-coordinate acceptance intervals.
support: Output arithmetic is adequate but many fitting/transfer recipes fail. Exact duplicate-row counts do not measure within-cell information loss. This tests a possible cause, not an established explanation.
selection: First four common50k rows in each of four snapshots, fixed existing order. Separate seed-specific input cells. For each row select the positive non-N2/non-AR species and direction with largest mass transfer to/from N2 permitted by both FP32 cells. Use one-quarter cell room; at most eight halvings only to establish exact encoding equality. No chemical-result selection.
physics: Fixed temperature and initial pressure, fixed-volume fixed-temperature evolution over1e-6s. Composition transfer conserves mass and nonnegativity. Tiny local input perturbations are diagnostic challenge states only, not new training labels or an expanded operating domain.
reference: Reuse three CVODE endpoint checks and two independently formulated Radau increment checks. Empirical uncertainty=max discrepancy plus endpoint-spacing floor, not a certified bound. Require all five solves. Compare intended and Cantera-effective initial composition encodings.
decision: A qualified incompatible pair requires bit-identical FP32 normalized network inputs, nonzero physical perturbation, both component uncertainty<=0.1 allowance, and disjoint outward-expanded GBCT normalized-output intervals. Account for tolerance variation under reference uncertainty and full saturation preimage. Any support motivates a separately registered precision-controlled experiment. No cases does not prove quantization harmless or justify an unregistered larger search.
controls: Original versus perturbed states; both primary seed preprocessing maps separately. Original labels remain untouched. No U, development, restricted confirmation or candidate weights are evaluated. No training or promotion.
